description: Shared Renovate preset for the Gravixar fleet (gravixar-sv). One place to tune dependency automation for every repo. Public repo so BOTH public and private consumers can resolve it. Consume with: { "extends": ["github>gravixar-sv/renovate-config"] }. SCHEDULE (HQ S296, 2026-11-04, task fleet-renovate-update-only-on-schedule): Renovate opens, updates, rebases and auto-merges its branches only on Mondays, Pakistan time (timezone Asia/Karachi, cron '* * * * 1'; the old schedule:weekly preset was 00:00-03:59 UTC). updateNotScheduled=false stops the re-pushes outside that window: under Renovate's default (true) an open PR was re-pushed all week whenever a newer version came out, and every push re-ran CI and a Vercel preview. Renovate was 42% of the fleet's October GitHub Actions spend ($11.79 of $28.18, Oct 1-25; robonamix all-minor-patch 51 runs, ace-of-maids 64). The window is the whole Monday, not a 4-hour slot, because with updateNotScheduled=false Renovate also skips AUTO-MERGE outside the window (lib/workers/repository/update/branch/index.ts returns 'update-not-scheduled' before any automerge check) and the Mend app runs each repo about every 4 hours: robonamix #212 (weekly group) opened 01:16Z and merged itself at 05:40Z on 2026-11-02, the next run, which a 4-hour window would have skipped, leaving a green PR for a week. Security PRs are untouched: Renovate forces vulnerabilityAlerts' own empty schedule onto them, so they still open, rebase and merge at any hour. Ticking a PR's rebase box or a Dependency Dashboard checkbox still acts at once.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security PRs merge themselves once EVERY status check on the PR is green. platformAutomerge=false makes Renovate check the branch status itself instead of handing the PR to GitHub auto-merge, so a repo with no required checks still waits for its Vercel and CI checks. Before this (HQ S250, 2026-10-15) a green security PR waited days for a person: 5 sat in /fleet triage at once. A repo whose every merge needs a person opts out in its own renovate.json with vulnerabilityAlerts.automerge=false (bs-hub does). Majors stay human. The weekly all-non-major group follows the same rule since HQ S254 (packageRules below).

lockFileMaintenance.description: The weekly lockfile refresh re-resolves every transitive dependency inside its declared range, which clears most transitive advisories (brace-expansion, source-map-js, fast-uri) without an override pin. It merges itself once every check is green, with the same rules and the same per-repo opt-out as vulnerabilityAlerts (HQ S250). Window (HQ S296, 2026-11-04, task fleet-renovate-update-only-on-schedule): the whole Monday, Pakistan time, like every other branch. It was 'before 6am on monday' (UTC) in Renovate's deprecated later.js text syntax; cron replaces it, and the window is wider so that, under updateNotScheduled=false, the PR can still merge itself on a later run the same day (robonamix #213 opened 05:41Z and merged itself 08:39Z on 2026-11-02, after a 6am cut-off). minimumReleaseAge does not apply here: the npm rule below matches major/minor/patch only, so this branch's stability check can never sit pending.

packageRules.description: @gravixar-sv/core is published to a private registry that Renovate's public lookup cannot resolve; its versioning is managed outside Renovate. Disable to remove the fleet-wide no-result warning.

Override blocks (npm `overrides`, package.json `pnpm.overrides`, pnpm-workspace.yaml `overrides`, yarn `resolutions`) are a SECURITY-REMEDIATION surface, not a dependency surface. Every entry is a version-scoped floor chosen to clear one advisory without breaking the transitive consumer it rewrites, so version currency is the wrong driver. Renovate only ever proposes raising the VALUE while the KEY stays (gravixar-hq #787: '@hono/node-server@<1.19.15' -> '^2.0.0'; robonamix #149: 'undici@<6.27.0' -> '^8.0.0'): a no-op today, and the day something matches the key it forces a MAJOR onto a consumer that declared a caret range. On npm repos the in-range lockfile bump of an override also fails Renovate's artifact step outright (blood-donate-app #36: 'EOVERRIDE Override for fast-uri@3.1.7 conflicts with direct dep'). Entries change only when an advisory drives them (Cortex security rollups / audit gates). Promoted fleet-wide 2026-09-13 from the per-repo rules in gravixar-hq and bs-hub (decision bs-hub-renovate-excludes-overrides).

typescript stays on the 6.x line fleet-wide (decision deferred-typescript-7-blocked-upstream, until 2026-11-30). 7.x is the native Go compiler. Next.js >= 16.3.3 now type-checks on it (gravixar-hq #852's own Vercel build ran 'Running TypeScript ... Finished TypeScript in 3.2s' with typescript@7.0.2 resolved), so the binding blocker moved to typescript-eslint: 8.68-8.70 declare peer 'typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0' and throw 'typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0' at load, which kills every repo's `eslint` run (reproduced in gravixar-hq on 2026-09-13; bs-hub #531 hit the same wall). `next build` does not run eslint, so a green Vercel check does not cover this. Minor/patch inside 6.x keeps flowing. Lift by deleting this rule once `npm view typescript-eslint peerDependencies.typescript` admits 7.x (tracking typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint#10940) and one repo's lint + typecheck + build all pass on 7.x.

eslint stays on the 9.x line fleet-wide (decision deferred-eslint-10-blocked-upstream). eslint-config-next (16.3.5 at the time of writing) bundles eslint-plugin-react 7.37.5, whose peer range stops at ^9.7 and which crashes at rule execution under eslint 10 (context.getFilename was removed; gravixar-hq #851 CI 2026-09-10, bs-hub #516, robonamix #39). `next build` does not run eslint, so a green Vercel check does not cover this. Lift by deleting this rule once eslint-plugin-react declares a ^10 peer AND eslint-config-next bundles that release.

npm releases must be 3 days old before Renovate proposes them (HQ S296, 2026-11-04, task fleet-renovate-update-only-on-schedule). Why: a burst of patch releases (next, @types/*, ai) lands as ONE push instead of one push per release, each of which re-ran CI and a Vercel preview; and npm lets an author unpublish within 72 hours, so a 3-day-old version is also safer to build on. Same values as Renovate's own security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm preset, written out here so the reason travels with the rule. internalChecksFilter=strict (Renovate's default since v42, set explicitly) means a too-young version is left OUT of the branch rather than pushed with a pending 'renovate/stability-days' check, so a branch only exists once every version in it has aged, the check is already green, and auto-merge is never left waiting on it; young versions show under 'Pending Status Checks' on the Dependency Dashboard, where a tick forces them. Security PRs are NOT delayed: Renovate forces vulnerabilityAlerts' own config (minimumReleaseAge null) onto them (docs key-concepts/minimum-release-age: 'Security updates bypass any minimumReleaseAge checks'). Lock file maintenance is NOT matched (it has no release timestamp, so it would sit pending forever under Renovate 42's timestamp-required default).

Majors wait on the Dependency Dashboard: Renovate lists each one as a checkbox on the repo's 'Dependency Dashboard' issue and opens no branch, PR, CI run or Vercel preview until someone ticks it (HQ S296, 2026-11-04, task fleet-renovate-update-only-on-schedule). Why: majors never merge themselves, so an open major PR only waits, and every Renovate touch rebuilt it; 20 non-security major PRs sat open fleet-wide on 2026-11-04, several since September (ubuntu 26, gradle 9, stripe 23, ai 7, pnpm 10/12, @sentry/nextjs 11, node 26), and they also use up prConcurrentLimit (5) slots: robonamix's 4 open majors plus the weekly group made 5 on 2026-11-02, and its lockfile refresh opened only after the group merged. Security fixes that happen to be majors still open at once (vulnerabilityAlerts forces dependencyDashboardApproval=false). This gates only NEW branches: a major PR that is already open stays open and keeps updating on Mondays until it is merged or closed (lib/workers/repository/update/branch/index.ts checks approval only when the branch does not exist). Closing one moves it to the dashboard's closed/ignored list, where a tick brings it back.

The weekly all-non-major group (group:allNonMajor) merges itself once EVERY status check on the PR is green, like security PRs and the lockfile refresh. Decided by Qamar in HQ S254 (2026-10-17, task renovate-automerge-non-major-proposal): HQ's group PR sat red for 12 days and green ones waited days for a click that added no judgement; the checks are the gate either way. platformAutomerge is false at the TOP of this preset so Renovate checks the branch status itself on every auto-merge path: GitHub's native auto-merge would merge at once on a repo with no required checks (gravixar-hq allows auto-merge and requires none). Majors stay human. A repo where every merge needs a person opts out in its own renovate.json with a LAST packageRule { matchUpdateTypes: [minor, patch], automerge: false } (bs-hub does). recreateWhen=always (HQ S276, 2026-10-28): the group PR has the SAME branch and title every week, so under the top-level recreateWhen=never Renovate found last week's automerged PR, took this one for a repeat and switched automerge OFF (PR body: 'Automerge: Disabled because a matching PR was automerged previously'; renovate lib/workers/repository/update/branch/index.ts + check-existing.ts). That is why green group PRs from 2026-09-28 still waited for a click in HQ, Robonamix, BloodLink and Broomstick. Majors keep never, so a major you close stays closed.
